stories.headline: Houthi forces capture Yemeni port city of Mokha as crude oil prices surge past $100
stories.body:
Houthi forces captured the Yemeni port city of Mokha from Saudi-backed forces [c10]. The port city sits about 80 kilometers, or 50 miles, from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait [c9]. Pro-government commander Tarek Salah said his forces moved their command center on the west coast to a safe location [c11]. A Yemeni military source told AFP that Houthi forces were pushing towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait [c5]. Fighting started again in Yemen as Houthi forces moved south towards the Bab al-Mandab Strait [c8].

A Yemeni military source told AFP that Houthi fighters also captured Zuqar Island in the Red Sea [c12]. They took the island after rocket barrages and a boat assault [c12]. Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi warplanes carried out 64 air strikes across four western Yemeni provinces within 24 hours [c13]. Saudi authorities reported that Houthi missile and drone strikes on September 8 injured 73 civilians [c14]. They said the strikes also temporarily stopped operations at multiple oil facilities [c14].

The fighting caused global oil prices to jump sharply. The benchmark US oil contract West Texas Intermediate rose above $100 a barrel on September 10 after Houthis seized Mocha [c1]. Brent crude rose more than 6 percent past $107 a barrel on September 10 [c2]. That was its highest level since May [c2]. Rystad Energy analyst Jorge Leon said oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz dropped [c6]. It fell from around 8 million barrels per day in late August to between 1.5 million and 2 million barrels per day [c6].

Financial markets reacted to the news as well. The 30-year US Treasury bond yield reached 5.36 percent [c3]. This marked a new peak since 2007 [c3]. US producer price inflation climbed to 5.4 percent in August [c4]. That was up from 4.8 percent in July [c4]. The European Central Bank increased its benchmark interest rate to 2.5 percent on September 10 [c7].

vocab.meaning: Heavy continuous attacks using rockets, artillery, or missiles.
The financial return or interest paid on an investment.

stories.headline: Cargo ship fire at Qingdao port in China kills 25 people
stories.body:
Chinese state media CCTV reported 25 people died in a fire on a foreign-flagged cargo ship in Qingdao, China [c16]. At least 25 people were killed after a fire broke out aboard a ship at a shipyard in China [c15]. Five people remain missing after the cargo vessel fire at the shipyard in Qingdao [c22].

There were 42 people on board the vessel [c17]. Seventeen people were evacuated from the ship [c17]. Five people were hospitalized in stable condition [c17].

The ship involved in the fire was named the Ocean Melody [c19]. It is a 190-meter Liberia-flagged carrier that arrived in Qingdao on August 31 [c19]. The fire began around 11:15 local time during maintenance work [c18]. Firefighters put out the blaze just over three hours later [c18].

Chinese President Xi Jinping told authorities to thoroughly investigate fire hazards [c20]. President Xi instructed officials to strictly hold responsible parties to account [c20]. A shipyard explosion in Fujian province in August killed a rescue worker and injured 12 people [c21].

vocab.meaning: Moved away from a dangerous place to a safe location.
Work done to keep equipment or buildings in good condition.

stories.headline: Republicans hold midterm convention in Dallas as Donald Trump proposes $5,000 checks
stories.body:
Republican National Committee chair Joe Gruters opened the second night of the party's midterm convention in Dallas [c23]. The event marked the one-year anniversary of Charlie Kirk's death [c23]. Republicans gathered in Dallas to close their midterm convention before upcoming elections [c27].

House Speaker Mike Johnson warned delegates that swing-seat Democrats vote with socialists [c24]. Johnson said communists will be in Congress next year [c24]. Donald Trump told CBS News he does not believe Congress needs to approve proposed $5,000 checks for Americans [c26]. Distributing $5,000 checks to all 276.8 million American adults would cost about $1.384 trillion [c30].

The US government collected a record $195 billion in customs duties during fiscal year 2025 [c31]. The US has brought in about $475 billion in tariff and excise tax revenue since early 2025 [c32]. Over $100 billion was refunded after Supreme Court rulings [c32].

Prosecutor Joe diGenova resigned from leading a Justice Department inquiry [c25]. The inquiry targeted former government officials who investigated Donald Trump [c25]. Democratic Senator John Fetterman made a surprise virtual address at the convention [c28]. Fetterman praised Republican Senator Dave McCormick [c28]. Pennsylvania state Representative Malcolm Kenyatta criticized Fetterman [c29]. Kenyatta called Fetterman the laziest Benedict Arnold America has seen and called on him to resign [c29].

vocab.meaning: A large official meeting of a political party.
Taxes paid on goods brought into a country.

stories.headline: August 2026 recorded as joint-hottest month globally as El Nino grows
stories.body:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service reported August 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally [c33]. It tied with July 2023 [c33]. August 2026 was 1.65 degrees Celsius warmer than the estimated 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline [c34].

Europe's climate monitor reported an unprecedented El Nino pattern is continuing to grow globally [c36]. Daily global extra-polar sea surface temperature reached a record high of 21.11 degrees Celsius in August 2026 [c37]. Major European rivers experienced exceptionally low flows during August [c38]. These rivers included the Rhine, Danube, Southern Bug, and Dnieper [c38].

India recorded a mean monthly temperature of 28.01 degrees Celsius in August 2026 [c35]. This made it the country's warmest August since 1901 [c35].

In the contiguous US, June through August 2026 averaged 74.37 degrees Fahrenheit, or 23.54 degrees Celsius [c39]. This broke the 1936 Dust Bowl record by nearly 0.4 degrees Fahrenheit [c39].

vocab.meaning: A starting point or standard level used for comparison.

stories.headline: Israeli military destroys Hezbollah tunnel network in southern Lebanon
stories.body:
Israeli forces destroyed Hezbollah tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon on September 10 [c40]. Israel's military said it destroyed a network of Hezbollah tunnels located on the ridge [c42].

The US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 4.1 tremor in southern Lebanon [c41]. The tremor occurred near the tunnel destruction site [c41].

Israel also expanded its presence in South Lebanon [c43]. UN peacekeepers escorted NPR journalists behind Israeli lines during the operation [c43].

vocab.meaning: A mild shaking of the ground or an earthquake.
Accompanied someone to offer protection or guidance.

stories.headline: School fire in eastern DR Congo leaves at least 24 children dead
stories.body:
Twenty-four schoolchildren died during a stampede while fleeing a fire at two schools in Bukavu in the Democratic Republic of Congo [c44]. Authorities confirmed at least 14 schoolchildren were killed in the fire that swept through the schools [c49]. A hospital in Bukavu admitted over 50 students from the fire, 14 of whom died [c48]. South Kivu Vice Governor Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge reported 19 girls and five boys were killed [c47]. Vice Governor Bwenge added that 29 people were injured [c47].

The fire destroyed about 300 houses in Bukavu's Kadutu commune [c45]. M23 rebels previously captured the South Kivu provincial capital of Bukavu in February 2025 [c46].

vocab.meaning: A sudden rushed movement of a crowd of frightened people.
Swept over and completely covered something.

stories.headline: BRICS Summit begins in New Delhi as Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping arrive
stories.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin landed in New Delhi on Friday to attend the BRICS summit [c50, c51]. He arrived for a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi [c50]. The BRICS Summit 2026 marks Putin's first overseas participation in a BRICS summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 [c52]. PM Modi and President Putin previously met in Bishkek on August 31 on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit [c53].

The 18th BRICS summit is taking place at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from September 12-13 [c61, c68]. Its theme is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability' [c68].

Many global leaders are expected to attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi [c62]. Expected guests include Chinese President Xi Jinping, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto [c62]. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to attend [c64]. This marks his first visit to India since taking office after President Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in 2024 [c64]. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, WHO head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala are also attending [c63]. But Bangladesh will not be represented at the summit [c65]. Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir confirmed this despite an invitation sent to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman [c65].

India and Russia are expanding economic and defense discussions. Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia and India are exploring cooperation in rare earths [c54]. Peskov said Russia is exploring the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India [c54]. Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu confirmed expanded talks on manufacturing aircraft in India [c55]. These include the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100 [c55]. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India and Russia aim to reach $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 [c66]. Goyal said the countries also target $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030 [c66]. Bilateral trade between India and Russia currently stands at around $60 billion [c67].

Delhi authorities put strict security measures in place. Special airspace restrictions apply from September 11 to September 13 within 300 kilometers of New Delhi [c56]. Safdarjung Airport will remain closed, except for specified military and police helicopter operations [c59]. Aircraft climbing near the restricted zone must reach around 29,000 feet by the time they are 200 kilometers from the capital [c60]. Normal scheduled commercial flights at Delhi's main airport will continue taking off and landing [c57]. Nearly 4,800 traffic personnel are deployed in Delhi for security and traffic management [c58].

vocab.meaning: The portion of the atmosphere controlled by a country above its territory.

stories.headline: Delhi authorities seal Chandni Chowk shops following fatal Satya Niketan building collapse
stories.body:
Municipal workers sealed 56 jewellery and bullion shops in Chandni Chowk's Kucha Mahajani on Thursday [c70]. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi enforcement drive was intensified after a building collapse in Satya Niketan on September 6 left seven people dead [c71]. The five-storey paying guest building collapsed, killing seven people and injuring 12 [c73]. Five of the seven people killed were Delhi University students [c74].

Initial findings revealed the 50-year-old building in Satya Niketan had five floors despite only two floors being permitted [c75]. Police arrested the building owner, his son, the operator, and a contractor [c76]. Operator Shubham Tyagi was denied anticipatory bail by a Delhi court [c69].

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi suspended five municipal officials over alleged negligence [c77]. Three additional engineers were suspended for negligence after the collapse [c81]. The All India Bullion and Jewellers Association questioned whether only traders will bear the brunt or if action will also be taken against government departments and politicians [c72].

A Supreme Court Bench directed authorities across India to file affidavits on compliance regarding unauthorized constructions [c78]. Amicus curiae Ajit Kumar Sinha brought the Satya Niketan collapse to the Supreme Court's attention [c79]. The Delhi High Court scheduled further hearings on public interest litigation for September 25 [c80].

vocab.meaning: Done in preparation for something expected to happen.
Written legal statements confirmed by oath for court use.
